q: Bitly（短链服务）设计中，哪些属于核心功能需求？（多选）
q_en: Which features are core functional requirements for designing a Bitly-style URL shortener?
options: 提交长 URL，拿到一个短链（可选自定义别名和过期时间）
通过短链访问原始长 URL（重定向）
用户注册与账号管理
点击量、地域分布等分析功能
why: 核心功能只有两条：缩短（含可选别名/过期）和重定向。账号体系和点击分析都划到 below the line——它们加复杂度但不是短链的本质。
why_en: The core functions are just shortening a URL with optional alias and expiration and redirecting via the short link, while auth and analytics are out of scope.
options_en: Submit a long URL and get back a short link, optionally with a custom alias and expiration date.
Visit the short link and get redirected to the original long URL.
User registration and account management.
Analytics such as click counts and geographic breakdown.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户自己指定的短码，替代系统自动生成的短码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A custom alias is a short code the user picks instead of one the system generates.

optionExplanations: 这是短链的创建动作本身：接收长 URL，可选绑定别名或过期时间，是产品必须有的入口。
重定向让短链真正有用——没有它，短码只是个打不开的字符串。
账号体系管的是身份识别，不影响短链创建和跳转能不能跑起来，属于加分项而非核心。
点击分析是事后洞察，缺了它短链照样能跑，所以先放到 below the line。
optionExplanations_en: This is creation itself: submit the long URL with an optional alias or expiration, the entry point the product needs.
Redirecting is the whole point of a short link; without it the code is just a string that goes nowhere.
Accounts handle identity, not creation or redirect, so it is a nice-to-have, not core to shortening a URL.
Click analytics is after-the-fact insight; the shortener still works without it, so it stays below the line.
scenario: 面试只有 35 分钟设计 short.ly（1 亿日活、10 亿存量链接），范围必须先砍到最小可用集。
scenario_en: You have 35 minutes to design short.ly for 100M daily users and a billion stored links, so scope has to be cut to a minimal viable set first.

q: 补全 Bitly 的核心非功能需求：
q_en: Fill in Bitly's core non-functional requirements.
text: 短码必须{{唯一}}（一个短码只对应一个长 URL）；重定向延迟 < {{100}}ms；可用性 {{99.99}}%（可用性优先于一致性）；规模支持 {{10 亿}}条短链和 {{1 亿}} DAU。
why: 这四条 NFR 是后面所有深挖的锚点：唯一性驱动短码生成方案，低延迟驱动缓存/CDN，高可用驱动副本，规模数字驱动容量估算。
why_en: The non-functional requirements are unique short codes, sub-hundred-millisecond redirects, four-nines availability favoring availability over consistency, one billion URLs, and one hundred million daily active users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数，一天内至少使用一次产品的用户数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU is daily active users, the count of users who use the product at least once that day.

q: Bitly 的 NFR 里写「availability > consistency」，这句话的含义是？
q_en: What does availability greater than consistency mean in Bitly's non-functional requirements?
options: 必须强一致，宁可拒绝请求也不能返回旧数据
可用性和一致性要同时做到完全极致
优先保证可用，接受数据短暂不一致（CAP 选 AP）
这个系统的设计与 CAP 定理无关
why: 短链是读服务，用户拿不到重定向比读到一条稍旧的映射更糟，所以在分区/故障时优先可用。这也解释了为什么可以大胆用缓存和副本。
why_en: Choosing availability over consistency means the service keeps serving redirects even if some data is briefly stale, which justifies heavy caching and replication.
options_en: The system must stay strongly consistent even if that means rejecting requests.
Both availability and consistency must be pushed to their absolute limits at once.
It favors availability and accepts briefly stale data, an AP choice under CAP.
This system's design has nothing to do with the CAP theorem.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分区容错下，一致性和可用性只能二选一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says that under a network partition, a distributed system must trade off consistency against availability.

optionExplanations: 这其实是选 CP：金融转账这类不能读到旧值的系统才会这么做，短链读服务没必要为此牺牲可用性。
CAP 定理里分区发生时一致性和可用性只能二选一，两头拉满是个不存在的选项。
对，短链宁可让用户读到几秒前的旧映射，也不要直接拒绝服务——这就是 AP 的取舍。
任何跨节点的分布式系统一旦发生网络分区都逃不开 CAP，短链也不例外。
optionExplanations_en: That's picking CP — only systems like a bank ledger that can't serve stale reads need it; here it costs uptime for nothing.
Under a partition CAP forces a choice; pushing both consistency and availability to the max is not actually on the table.
Right — short links would rather serve a mapping that is a few seconds stale than refuse the redirect, which is the AP tradeoff.
Any distributed system spanning nodes hits CAP once a partition happens; this one is no exception.
scenario: short.ly 每天 1 亿次重定向；机房分区时只能二选一：继续跳转，或保证读到最新映射。
scenario_en: short.ly serves 100M redirects a day, and during a partition you must pick one: keep redirecting, or guarantee the freshest mapping.

q: 这个读写比对数据库选型和优化重点最直接的含义是什么？
q_en: What does this read-write ratio imply for database choice and optimization focus?
options: 必须选择专门为高写吞吐设计的数据库（如宽列存储）
写路径几乎不构成瓶颈，优化预算应集中在读路径的缓存与索引
应该给写路径也加多级缓存来分担压力
读写比不影响架构决策，索引和缓存同等重要即可
why: 写入量极小，几乎任何数据库都扛得住；1000:1 的读写比意味着优化预算该压在读路径的缓存和索引上。
why_en: Writes are tiny in volume, so almost any database can handle them; a 1000:1 read-write ratio means the optimization budget belongs on read-path caching and indexing.
scenario: Bitly 的点击（读）与新建短链（写）之比约为 1000:1；写入端每天新建量级只有个位到两位数 QPS。
scenario_en: Bitly has roughly a 1000:1 read-to-write ratio, and new short-link creation is only single- to low-double-digit QPS.
options_en: We must choose a database built for very high write throughput, such as a wide-column store.
The write path is barely a bottleneck, so optimization budget should go to caching and indexing the read path.
We should add multi-level caching to the write path too.
The read-write ratio doesn't affect the architecture; indexing and caching matter equally.
optionExplanations: 宽列存储是为每秒海量写入准备的，这里写入量只有个位数 QPS，选它是杀鸡用牛刀。
对，1000:1 的读写比意味着写路径几乎闲着，把预算全砸在读路径缓存和索引上才划算。
写路径本来就轻，加缓存只会多一层失效和一致性维护成本，收益不成正比。
读写比正是决定优化预算怎么分配的关键信号，忽视它会导致精力用错地方。
optionExplanations_en: Wide-column stores are built for massive write throughput; with single-digit write QPS here, that is overkill.
Right — a 1000:1 ratio means the write path is barely busy, so the budget belongs on read-path caching and indexing.
The write path is already light; caching it just adds invalidation overhead for little payoff.
The read-write ratio is exactly the signal that should steer optimization budget; ignoring it misallocates effort.

q: 「读远多于写」这个观察，对 Bitly 设计最直接的影响是？
q_en: What is the main design implication of Bitly being far more read-heavy than write-heavy?
options: 必须换成强一致数据库，否则无法上线
必须优先对写路径做分片
应该去掉索引以减少写放大
读路径要激进缓存、读写分开扩展
why: 极端偏读意味着把优化火力集中在读路径：缓存、CDN、读服务独立扩容；写路径每秒约 1 行，几乎任何数据库都扛得住。
why_en: The extreme read skew means aggressive caching and independently scaled read paths matter most, making this a textbook scaling-reads problem.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Clicks["大量点击"] --> Read["Read Service 横向扩展"]
    Read --> Cache["缓存热门短码"]
    Cache -->|miss| DB[("Mapping DB")]
    Writes["少量创建"] --> Write["Write Service"]
    Write --> DB
options_en: We must switch to a strongly consistent database or the system cannot ship.
We must shard the write path first.
We should drop indexes to cut write amplification.
The read path needs aggressive caching, and reads and writes should scale separately.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门针对读多写少场景的扩展模式，靠缓存和只读副本分担压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scaling reads is a pattern for read-heavy systems that leans on caching and read replicas to absorb load.

optionExplanations: 一致性要求和读写比是两回事，读多写少不代表非要强一致数据库不可。
写入每秒才约 1 行，分片写路径解决的是写入量大的问题，这里根本用不上。
索引服务的正是读路径查找，为了省一点写入成本去掉它，会直接拖垮重定向延迟。
对，读远多于写时把火力放在缓存和读服务独立扩容，才是真正对症的优化。
optionExplanations_en: Consistency and read-write ratio are separate axes; being read-heavy doesn't force a strongly consistent database.
Writes run at roughly one row per second; sharding the write path solves a high-write-volume problem this system lacks.
The index exists to serve read lookups; dropping it to save a little write cost would wreck redirect latency instead.
Right — when reads dwarf writes, pouring effort into caching and independently scaling the read service is the actual fix.
scenario: short.ly 读写比约 1000:1，写入约每秒 1 行，重定向 P99 预算 100ms。
scenario_en: short.ly runs about a 1000:1 read-to-write ratio, roughly one write per second, with a 100ms P99 budget on redirects.

q: Bitly 的核心实体（core entities）是哪一组？
q_en: Which set contains Bitly's core entities?
options: 短链、点击事件、广告
原始长 URL、短 URL、用户
用户、会话、支付
长 URL、DNS 记录、证书
why: 实体阶段只需要一个简短清单：原始长 URL、短 URL、创建它的用户。列出来对齐思路即可，字段细节留到高层设计再补。
why_en: The core entities are simply the original long URL, the short URL, and the user who created it.
options_en: Short link, click event, advertisement.
Original long URL, short URL, and the user.
User, session, payment.
Long URL, DNS record, certificate.
optionExplanations: 点击事件和广告属于分析/变现层的实体，创建-重定向这条主路径压根没用到它们。
对，创建和跳转这条主路径只需要长 URL、短 URL 和创建者这三个对象，够用了。
会话和支付是账号/交易类产品的实体，短链主路径不涉及登录态或计费。
DNS 记录和证书属于网络基础设施层，不是短链业务要建模的数据对象。
optionExplanations_en: Click events and ads belong to the analytics/monetization layer; the create-and-redirect path never touches them.
Right — creating and following a link only needs three objects: the long URL, the short URL, and the user who made it.
Sessions and payments are entities for login and billing products; the core shortener path involves neither.
DNS records and certificates live in the network infrastructure layer, not a data object the shortener needs to model.
scenario: short.ly 只认两条功能需求：创建短链、重定向；实体清单要刚好覆盖这两条路径。
scenario_en: short.ly has only two functional requirements — create a short link and redirect — so the entity list should cover exactly those two paths.

scenario: 要设计「缩短 URL」的 REST 接口：客户端提交长 URL（可带自定义别名、过期时间），服务端在数据库里新建一条短码到长 URL 的映射。
scenario_en: You are designing the REST endpoint for shortening a URL: the client submits a long URL, optional alias, and expiration, and the server creates a new code-to-URL mapping.
q: 应该用哪个 HTTP 方法？
q_en: Which HTTP method should this endpoint use?
options: GET /urls?long_url=...
PUT /urls
POST /urls
DELETE /urls
why: 缩短 URL 是在数据库里「创建一条新资源」（长短映射），REST 里创建用 POST；请求体带 long_url、可选 custom_alias 和 expiration_date，返回 short_url。
why_en: Shortening creates a new mapping resource, so a POST to /urls with the long URL and optional alias and expiration is the right verb.
whenOtherWins: 如果是更新已有短链（比如改过期时间）才用 PUT；读取用 GET；REST 面试里 9/10 的情况就是按「动词对操作」选。
options_en: GET /urls?long_url=...
PUT /urls
POST /urls
DELETE /urls
tradeoff: 创建新资源用 POST vs 更新已有资源用 PUT

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用 HTTP 方法表达资源操作的 API 设计风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that maps HTTP verbs onto operations on resources.

optionExplanations: GET 用来读取已有资源，查询某条已存在的映射详情时才用它，创建新映射不该用它。
PUT 用在客户端已知完整资源标识、要整体覆盖或更新时，比如改一个已有短链的过期时间。
对，缩短 URL 是在建一条全新的短码到长链映射，REST 里创建资源正是 POST 的语义。
DELETE 用来撤销一条已存在的短链，这里是创建新映射，方向正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: GET reads an existing resource — fine for looking up a mapping you already have, wrong for creating one.
PUT fits when the client already knows the full resource id and wants to overwrite it, like updating an existing link's expiration.
Right — shortening a URL creates a brand-new code-to-URL mapping, and POST is REST’s verb for creating a resource.
DELETE removes an existing short link; here we're creating a new mapping, the opposite direction.

q: 补全缩短 URL 的请求与响应：
q_en: Fill in the request and response for shortening a URL.
text: POST /urls 请求体包含 {{long_url}}、可选的 {{custom_alias}} 和可选的 {{expiration_date}}；响应返回 {{short_url}}。重定向接口是 GET /{short_code}，返回 HTTP {{302}} 跳转。
why: API 通常与功能需求 1:1 对应：一个 POST 创建映射，一个 GET 做重定向。把可选参数（别名、过期）放进请求体，契约就完整了。
why_en: The API is a POST to /urls taking the long URL with optional alias and expiration and returning the short URL, plus a GET on the short code that answers with a 302 redirect.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 302 状态码，表示临时重定向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 302 is a status code meaning the resource is temporarily located elsewhere.

q: 用户访问 GET /{short_code} 后，浏览器是如何到达原始长 URL 的？
q_en: After a user visits GET /{short_code}, how does the browser reach the original long URL?
options: 服务器返回 Location 头的重定向，浏览器自动跟随
服务器代理抓取长 URL 页面内容再返回给用户
服务器返回一个带完整链接的 HTML 页面等用户点击
客户端用 JS 轮询接口拿到长 URL 后再跳转
why: 服务器查库拿到长 URL 后返回重定向响应（Location: 原始 URL），浏览器自动跳转——用户甚至不知道发生过一次重定向。
why_en: The server replies with an HTTP redirect carrying the long URL in the Location header, and the browser follows it automatically without the user noticing.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser
    participant S as Shortener
    participant DB as Mapping DB
    B->>S: GET /abc123
    S->>DB: lookup abc123
    DB-->>S: long_url
    S-->>B: 302 Location: long_url
    B->>B: follow redirect
options_en: The server replies with a redirect carrying a Location header, and the browser follows it automatically.
The server proxies and fetches the long URL's page content, then returns it.
The server returns an HTML page with the full link for the user to click.
The client polls an endpoint with JS to get the long URL, then navigates there.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 重定向响应里指明跳转目标地址的响应头。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Location header in an HTTP redirect response tells the browser where to go next.

optionExplanations: 对，服务器查到长 URL 后放进 Location 头返回重定向响应，浏览器自动跳转，用户全程无感。
这是反向代理才干的事：服务器帮用户抓取并转发页面内容，短链服务不需要碰目标站点的内容。
多一次人工点击只会拖慢体验，标准重定向本该在浏览器层自动完成，不需要用户确认。
轮询适合结果异步产生的场景，重定向查库很快，用轮询反而多绕一圈还更慢。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the server puts the long URL in a Location header and replies with a redirect; the browser follows it automatically.
That is what a reverse proxy does — fetching and forwarding page content. A shortener never needs to touch the destination content.
Forcing a manual click just adds friction; a standard redirect happens automatically at the browser layer.
Polling fits results that arrive asynchronously; a redirect lookup is fast, so polling just adds an extra round trip.
scenario: 用户点开 short.ly/abc123，跳转要对用户无感，且不能多渲染一个中间页面。
scenario_en: A user clicks short.ly/abc123; the jump has to feel invisible and must not render an extra interstitial page.

q: 在「浏览器是否缓存重定向」这个维度上，301 和 302 的区别是？
q_en: How do 301 and 302 differ in whether the browser caches the redirect?
options: 两者都会被浏览器缓存并跳过我们
302 会被缓存，301 反而不会
两者都不会被浏览器缓存
301 缓存后绕开我们，302 每次回源
why: 301 表示资源永久迁移，浏览器会记住并直接跳长 URL，流量绕开我们；302 表示临时位置，浏览器每次都先来问我们。这一个维度决定了控制权归属。
why_en: Browsers cache a permanent 301 and may skip our server on later visits, while a temporary 302 is not cached so every click still hits us.

rows: 后续可能绕过服务，难更新或统计
保留过期、修改和点击统计控制权

options_en: Both get cached by the browser and bypass us.
302 gets cached, but 301 does not.
Neither one gets cached by the browser.
A cached 301 bypasses us; a 302 always comes back to our server.
tradeoff: 301 让浏览器接管缓存换性能 vs 302 保留服务端控制权

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 301，表示资源永久搬走，浏览器通常会缓存这个跳转。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 301 signals a permanent move, and browsers typically cache that redirect.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 302，表示资源临时搬走，浏览器不缓存，每次都会回来问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 302 signals a temporary move, so browsers do not cache it and ask again each time.

optionExplanations: 302 是临时重定向，浏览器默认不缓存它，每次点击仍会先回到我们服务器。
说反了：会被缓存的是表示永久搬迁的 301，302 才是每次都要重新确认的那个。
301 表示永久搬迁，浏览器通常会记住并直接跳过我们，不是两个都不缓存。
对，301 被缓存后流量绕开我们，302 不被缓存所以每次都先经过我们服务器。
optionExplanations_en: A 302 is a temporary redirect and browsers do not cache it by default; every click still comes back to us first.
That is backwards — 301 signals a permanent move and gets cached; 302 is the one browsers re-check every time.
A 301 signals a permanent move and browsers typically remember it and skip us later, so neither is uncached.
Right — a cached 301 lets traffic bypass us, while an uncached 302 routes every click through our server first.
scenario: short.ly 的链接目标要能随时改、点击要能计数，所以在意浏览器会不会缓存这次重定向。
scenario_en: short.ly needs link targets to stay editable and clicks to stay countable, so whether the browser caches the redirect matters.

scenario: 短链服务希望以后还能修改/过期链接，并保留统计每次点击的能力（即使分析暂时超纲）。
scenario_en: The URL shortener still wants the ability to update or retire links later and count every click, even if analytics is out of scope for now.
q: 重定向应该返回哪种状态码？
q_en: Which status code should the redirect return?
options: 301 Moved Permanently
302 Found（临时重定向）
200 OK
404 Not Found
why: 302 不被浏览器缓存，每次点击都经过我们的服务器：既保留了更新/过期链接的控制权，也保留了统计点击的能力，是短链的常规选择。
why_en: A 302 keeps every click flowing through our server, preserving control to update or retire links, and the ability to count clicks.
whenOtherWins: 如果链接确定永不变更、且想靠浏览器缓存把延迟和服务器负载降到最低，301 更合适——代价是失去控制和统计。
options_en: 301 Moved Permanently.
302 Found, a temporary redirect.
404 Not Found.
tradeoff: 302 保留控制权和统计能力 vs 301 换浏览器缓存的性能

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 301，永久重定向，浏览器通常缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 301 is a permanent redirect that browsers typically cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 302，临时重定向，浏览器不缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 302 is a temporary redirect that browsers do not cache.

optionExplanations: 目标链接确定永不再变、且想靠浏览器缓存换取最低延迟时，301 才是更合适的选择。
对，短链还想保留改目标、让链接失效和统计点击的能力，302 不被缓存能让每次点击都回到我们服务器。
200 表示直接返回内容而不是跳转，这里客户端要拿到的是重定向指令，不是页面本身。
404 说明短码根本不存在，这里的短码是有效映射，只是要跳到另一个地址。
optionExplanations_en: A 301 only makes sense once the target is truly permanent and you want the browser cache to shave off latency.
Right — since the shortener still wants to update, retire, or count clicks on this link, an uncached 302 keeps every click routed through our server.
A 200 means returning content directly instead of redirecting; here the client needs a redirect instruction, not a body.
A 404 says the code does not exist at all; this code is a valid mapping that just points somewhere else.

q: 如果短链服务用了 301，会带来什么后果？
q_en: What happens if the URL shortener uses a 301 redirect?
options: 浏览器跳长 URL，链接失去更新/统计能力
重定向响应本身会变得明显更慢
浏览器会直接拒绝执行这次跳转
数据库的写入压力会因此明显增大
why: 301 一旦被浏览器缓存，之后的请求绕开我们的服务器：想改目标、让链接过期、或统计点击都做不到了。这就是短链偏爱 302 的原因。
why_en: Once a 301 is cached, later clicks bypass our server entirely, so we lose the ability to change, retire, or track that short link.
options_en: The browser jumps to the long URL, and the link loses its ability to be updated or tracked.
The redirect response itself becomes noticeably slower.
The browser directly refuses to follow the redirect.
Database write load rises noticeably because of it.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 301，永久重定向，浏览器通常会缓存这个跳转。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 301 is a permanent redirect that browsers typically cache.

optionExplanations: 对，浏览器把 301 记下来后之后的点击直接跳长 URL，绕开我们服务器，改目标或统计点击都做不到了。
状态码本身不影响单次响应速度，301 和 302 的查库和返回过程一样快。
301 是合法的重定向语义，浏览器会正常执行跳转，不存在拒绝执行的情况。
301 只影响后续读请求会不会经过我们，跟数据库写入压力没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Right — once the browser caches a 301, later clicks jump straight to the long URL, bypassing us, so we lose the ability to update it or count clicks.
The status code itself does not slow down a single response; the lookup and reply are just as fast either way.
A 301 is a valid redirect semantic and the browser follows it normally; there is no scenario where it refuses to.
A 301 only changes whether later reads route through us; it has nothing to do with database write load.
scenario: short.ly 用 301 上线一周后，点击统计几乎归零，改目标 URL 也对老用户不生效。
scenario_en: A week after short.ly shipped with 301s, click counts collapsed to near zero and editing a target URL stopped affecting existing users.

q: 用户访问了一个已过期的短链，服务器应返回？
q_en: What should the server return when a user visits an expired short link?
options: 302 照常跳转
500 Internal Server Error
410 Gone
301 到首页
why: 服务器查库后会拿当前时间和过期时间比较；已过期的短链返回 410 Gone，语义是「资源曾存在但已永久失效」。
why_en: For an expired short link the server compares the current date to the stored expiration and returns a 410 Gone status.
options_en: Return a normal 302 redirect.
Return a 500 Internal Server Error.
Return 410 Gone.
Return a 301 redirect to the homepage.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 410，表示资源曾经存在，但已经永久不可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 410 Gone means the resource used to exist but is now permanently unavailable.

optionExplanations: 302 意味着链接还有效只是临时跳转，一个已经过了有效期的短链继续这样回应会误导用户。
500 表示服务端出了故障，这里只是业务状态判断——查到了记录但已经超期，不是系统错误。
对，短链曾经存在但现在永久失效，410 的语义正好贴合这种「查得到但不该再用」的状态。
跳到首页会掩盖真实状态，用户不知道自己点的链接已经失效，还可能被当成正常跳转记录。
optionExplanations_en: A 302 implies the link is still live and this is just a hop; replying that way past the expiration window would mislead the user.
A 500 means the server itself broke; here it is a business check — we found the row, it is just past its window, not a failure.
Right — the link used to exist but is now permanently gone, and 410 is exactly the status for 'found it, but it's no longer usable.'
Redirecting to the homepage hides the real state — the user has no idea the link is gone, and it could even log as a normal hit.
scenario: short.ly 的营销短链设了 30 天过期，过期后爬虫和老用户仍在持续访问同一个短码。
scenario_en: short.ly gives marketing links a 30-day expiry, but crawlers and old users keep hitting the same code long after it lapses.

q: 把「创建短链」的处理流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the short-link creation flow in the correct order.
steps: 把短码（或别名）、长 URL、过期时间插入数据库
校验长 URL 格式（如 is-url 库）
生成短码；若用户给了自定义别名，先验证别名未被占用
把短 URL 返回给客户端
why: 顺序是：校验 → 生成短码（或用别名）→ 落库 → 返回。先校验能挡掉无效输入，短码生成是后面深挖的核心。
why_en: The creation flow validates the long URL, generates or accepts a short code, inserts the mapping into the database, and returns the short URL.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["客户端 POST /urls"] --> B["Primary Server
校验 URL 格式"] B --> C["生成短码 /
校验自定义别名"] C --> D[("数据库：短码→长URL
+过期时间")] D --> E["返回 short_url"]
tradeoff: 先校验挡掉脏输入 vs 先生成短码再校验的返工成本

q: 同一个长 URL 被多个用户提交时，为什么多数短链服务「不做去重」、允许多个短码指向同一长 URL？
q_en: Why do most URL shorteners avoid deduping the same long URL and allow multiple short codes for it?
options: 技术上完全做不到 URL 去重判断
不同用户想各自设过期和别名，去重会丢掉功能
去重会让新短码和旧短码发生严重冲突
数据库根本无法按长 URL 做查询
why: 去重省的只是存储：10 亿行 × ~500B ≈ 500GB，很便宜；但它同时砍掉了按用户各设过期、别名和分析的能力。
why_en: Deduping only saves storage — a billion rows times roughly 500 bytes is about 500GB, which is cheap — while costing per-user expiry, aliases, and analytics.
options_en: Deduplicating URLs is technically not possible at all.
Different users want their own expiration and alias, and dedup drops those.
Deduplication causes serious collisions between new and old short codes.
The database cannot query by long URL at all.
optionExplanations: 按 long_url 建个索引就能查重，技术上完全可行，不是这里不去重的原因。
对，去重意味着同一长 URL 永远返回同一短码，两个用户就没法各自设置不同的过期时间或别名了。
去重和短码冲突是两件事：冲突来自短码生成空间不够大，跟要不要复用长 URL 无关。
long_url 一样可以建索引查询，不去重的原因不是数据库能力受限。
optionExplanations_en: Indexing by long_url makes dedup lookup entirely feasible; that is not why this design skips it.
Right — deduping means the same long URL always returns the same code, so two users can no longer set their own expiration or alias on it.
Dedup and code collisions are unrelated: collisions come from too small a code space, not from reusing a long URL.
You can index by long_url just as easily; skipping dedup is not a database capability limit.
scenario: short.ly 每天新建 10 万条，同一个营销长 URL 常被不同用户分别提交并各设过期和别名。
scenario_en: short.ly creates 100k links a day, and the same marketing long URL is often submitted by different users each wanting their own expiry and alias.

scenario: 系统同时支持计数器生成的短码和用户自定义别名，担心未来某个计数器生成的短码恰好撞上已存在的自定义别名。
scenario_en: The system supports both counter-generated short codes and user-defined aliases, and you worry that a generated code could later collide with an existing alias.
q: 预防这种冲突的推荐做法是？
q_en: What is the recommended way to prevent this collision?
options: 每次生成短码后做一次全表扫描比对
干脆禁用自定义别名这个功能
让计数器从一个很大的数开始递增
给生成码加前缀、或用独立命名空间隔离两者
why: 用前缀字符或独立命名空间把「生成码」和「自定义别名」的取值空间隔开，两类短码天然不会相撞，无需运行时反复检查。
why_en: Prefix generated codes with a character custom aliases cannot use, or keep them in separate namespaces, so the two can never collide.
whenOtherWins: 如果别名功能流量极小，也可以只靠数据库 UNIQUE 约束兜底、冲突时报错重试——实现更简单，但把冲突留到了运行时。
options_en: Do a full table scan after generating every code to compare.
Just disable the custom alias feature entirely.
Start the counter from a very large number.
Prefix generated codes, or isolate them in a separate namespace from aliases.
tradeoff: 预先隔离取值空间 vs 运行时靠 UNIQUE 约束兜底重试

termDefinitions.meaning: 给不同来源的短码划分独立的取值范围，避免互相冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A namespace separates the value ranges of different code sources so they cannot collide.

optionExplanations: 表小或做离线校验时全表扫描还能凑合，但在线路径上每次生成都扫全表，延迟会随数据量线性变差。
禁用别名能规避冲突，但代价是砍掉一个产品功能，不是解决冲突问题的技术方案。
起点调大只是把计数器往后挪，别名取值范围没变，撞上大号别名的风险依然存在。
对，前缀或独立命名空间让两类短码的取值范围从一开始就不重叠，天然不用运行时检查。
optionExplanations_en: A full scan can pass for small tables or offline checks, but doing it on every online creation makes latency grow with data size.
Disabling aliases avoids the collision, but that cuts a product feature, not a technical fix for the collision.
Starting the counter higher just shifts its range further out — the alias space is untouched, so a collision is still possible.
Right — a prefix or separate namespace keeps the two code spaces from overlapping from the start, no runtime check needed.

q: 补全重定向的处理流程：
q_en: Fill in the redirect handling flow.
text: 浏览器发 GET /{short_code}；服务器在数据库里{{查找}}这个短码；找到且未{{过期}}（用当前时间对比过期时间）则取出长 URL，返回 {{302}} 重定向；已过期则返回 {{410}} Gone。
why: 重定向就是一次 key 查找加过期检查：命中未过期 → 302 跳转；过期 → 410。这条路径是全系统流量最大的路径，后面所有读优化都围绕它。
why_en: A redirect looks up the short code, checks the expiration date, and returns a 302 to the long URL or a 410 if the link has expired.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    Req["GET /{short_code}"] --> Lookup["按 short_code 查映射"]
    Lookup --> Found{"找到?"}
    Found -->|否| NotFound["404 Not Found"]
    Found -->|是| Expired{"已过期?"}
    Expired -->|是| Gone["410 Gone"]
    Expired -->|否| Redirect["302 Location: long_url"]

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 302，临时重定向状态码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 302 is the temporary-redirect status code.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 410 Gone，表示资源已永久失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 410 Gone means the resource is permanently unavailable.

q: 为什么所有短链请求天然会到达我们的服务器？
q_en: Why do all short-link requests naturally reach our server first?
options: 短链域名归我们所有，DNS 会路由到我们服务器
因为浏览器内置了专门处理短链的协议
因为我们提前在用户设备上预装了 SDK
因为用户的 ISP 专门做了特殊路由配置
why: 短链的关键前提：short.ly 是我们的域名，所以 short.ly/abc123 的每个请求都先落到我们的 Primary Server，我们才有机会查库并重定向。
why_en: Short URLs live on a domain we own, so every request to short dot l y naturally routes to our server where we can look up and redirect.
options_en: We own the short-link domain, and DNS routes requests to our server.
Because browsers have a protocol built in just for handling short links.
Because we preinstall an SDK on every user's device ahead of time.
Because the user's ISP applies special routing rules just for this.

termDefinitions.meaning: 域名系统，把域名解析成服务器地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS resolves a domain name into the server address that should handle the request.

optionExplanations: 对，short.ly 是我们注册的域名，DNS 解析天然把每个请求指到我们的服务器，这是重定向能生效的前提。
浏览器只认标准 HTTP，不存在专门为短链服务设计的浏览器协议。
重定向走的是普通网页请求，不需要用户设备上预装任何客户端组件。
路由到我们服务器靠的是域名解析，不需要也不依赖用户 ISP 做任何特殊配置。
optionExplanations_en: Right — short.ly is a domain we registered, so DNS naturally points every request at our server; that is the precondition for redirects.
Browsers only speak standard HTTP; there is no browser-native protocol built just for short links.
A redirect is just a normal web request; it needs no client component preinstalled on the user device.
Routing to our server comes from domain resolution — it does not need any special configuration from the user ISP.
scenario: short.ly 要对每次点击计数并有机会查库改写目标，前提是请求必须先落到我们的机器。
scenario_en: short.ly wants to count every click and get a chance to look up the target, which requires the request to land on our machines first.

q: 关于过期短链的清理，文章推荐的做法是？
q_en: What is the recommended cleanup approach for expired short links?
options: 每次读请求都同步扫描并删除所有过期行
永远不清理，让过期行一直留在表里
后台定期清理，TTL 设为 ≤ URL 过期时间
把清理工作交给用户手动删除
why: 清理走后台批处理即可，不占用请求路径；更关键的是缓存 TTL 要不长于 URL 过期时间，否则缓存里会残留已过期的映射继续跳转。
why_en: Clean up expired rows with a periodic background job and set cache TTLs at or below URL expiration so stale entries evict themselves.
options_en: Synchronously scan and delete all expired rows on every read request.
Never clean up, leaving expired rows in the table forever.
Run a periodic cleanup job, and cap TTL at or below the URL's expiration.
Make users delete their own expired links manually.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cache entry lives before it must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 把清理塞进读请求路径，会拖慢本该最快的重定向响应，得不偿失。
表只增不减，长期下来存储和索引都会被大量废弃行拖垮查询效率。
对，清理走后台批处理不占用请求路径，TTL 卡在过期时间之内还能防止缓存残留旧映射。
指望用户手动清理不可靠，大部分创建者根本不会回来处理已过期的短链。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming cleanup into the read path slows down what should be the fastest response in the system — not worth it.
The table only grows, and over time storage and index bloat from dead rows drags query performance down.
Right — a background batch job stays off the request path, and capping TTL at the expiration date stops cache from serving stale mappings.
Relying on users to clean up manually is unreliable; most creators never come back once a link has lapsed.
scenario: short.ly 存了 10 亿条映射且大量已过期，重定向 P99 预算 100ms，清理不能挤占请求路径。
scenario_en: short.ly holds a billion mappings with many already expired, and with a 100ms P99 redirect budget cleanup cannot sit on the request path.

q: Bitly 高层设计的三个核心组件及其职责，哪些描述正确？（多选）
q_en: Which descriptions correctly match the three core components in Bitly's high-level design?
options: Client：用户通过 Web/移动端与系统交互
Primary Server：接收请求，处理短码创建、校验等业务逻辑
Database：存短码到长 URL 的映射、别名和过期时间
Message Queue：所有读请求先排队
why: 最初的高层设计只需要三件套：客户端、承载业务逻辑的主服务器、存映射的数据库。消息队列在这个问题里并不需要——读是同步重定向。
why_en: The high-level design is just a client, a primary server holding the business logic, and a database storing the code-to-URL mappings.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Client Web/Mobile"] -->|POST create url| Server["Primary Server"]
    Client -->|GET short code| Server
    Server -->|create / lookup| DB[("Mapping DB")]
    Server -->|short_url or 302| Client
options_en: Client: users interact with the system through web or mobile.
Primary Server: receives requests and handles business logic like code creation and validation.
Database: stores the mapping of short codes to long URLs, aliases, and expiration dates.
Message Queue: every read request is queued first.
optionExplanations: 客户端是发起创建和重定向请求的入口，没有它系统就没有触达用户的路径。
主服务器扛住业务逻辑：校验 URL、生成或验证短码、协调数据库读写。
数据库是唯一的持久层，短码到长链的映射、别名、过期时间都得靠它扛住重启和故障。
重定向是同步查库直接返回的读请求，不存在需要排队削峰的写入洪峰，这里用不上队列。
optionExplanations_en: The client is the entry point for creation and redirect requests; without it there is no path to reach users.
The primary server carries the business logic: validating URLs, generating or checking codes, coordinating the database.
The database is the only durable layer — the mapping, alias, and expiration all need to survive restarts and failures.
Redirects are synchronous reads answered from a lookup; there is no write surge to smooth out, so a queue has no job here.
scenario: 白板上先画 short.ly 的最小可用架构：只支持创建短链和同步重定向，不做分析。
scenario_en: On the whiteboard you first sketch short.ly's minimal architecture: create a link and redirect synchronously, no analytics yet.

q: 设计短码生成方案时要同时满足哪些约束？（多选）
q_en: Which constraints must a short-code generation scheme satisfy at the same time?
options: 短码必须唯一
短码要尽可能短（毕竟是短链服务）
生成要高效（不能拖慢写入）
短码必须包含原 URL 的语义信息
why: 三条约束：唯一、短、高效——而且三者互相牵制（更长更不易撞但不「短」，查重保唯一但不「高效」）。语义可读性不是要求。
why_en: Short-code generation must balance three competing constraints: uniqueness, shortness, and efficient generation.
options_en: The short code must be unique.
The short code should be as short as possible.
Generation must be efficient and not slow down writes.
The short code must carry semantic meaning from the original URL.
optionExplanations: 唯一性是硬约束——两个长 URL 撞上同一个短码，重定向就会指错方向。
短是产品卖点本身，短码越长用户越懒得分享，失去了「短」链接的意义。
生成逻辑跑在写入路径上，算得慢就等于拖慢每一次创建请求的响应时间。
语义可读性从来不是要求，短码只是个查找键，可读性反而会让它变长。
optionExplanations_en: Uniqueness is a hard constraint — if two long URLs collide on one code, the redirect points to the wrong place.
Shortness is the whole pitch; a longer code makes users less likely to bother sharing it, defeating the point.
Generation sits on the write path, so a slow algorithm directly drags down every creation request's response time.
Semantic readability was never a requirement; the code is just a lookup key, and readability would only make it longer.
scenario: short.ly 每天新建 10 万条、存量 10 亿；短码要塞进 short.ly/xxx 且不能拖慢写入。
scenario_en: short.ly adds 100k links a day on top of a billion stored; the code must fit in short.ly/xxx without slowing writes.

q: 「直接取长 URL 的前 N 个字符当短码」这个方案为什么不可行？
q_en: Why is taking the first N characters of the long URL as the short code not viable?
options: 这种前缀方案生成短码的速度太慢
共享前缀的 URL 会映射到同一短码，破坏唯一性
前缀字符串没法做 base62 编码
浏览器不认识这种格式的短码
why: 比如所有 www.linkedin.com/in/... 的链接前 8 个字符都一样，会全部撞到同一个短码上——违反第一条约束「唯一」，方案直接出局。
why_en: Taking a URL prefix fails because any two URLs sharing the first characters map to the same code, destroying uniqueness.
options_en: This prefix approach is too slow at generating codes.
URLs sharing a prefix collapse onto the same short code, breaking uniqueness.
A prefix string cannot be Base62 encoded.
Browsers do not recognize this short-code format.
optionExplanations: 取前几个字符是最简单的字符串操作，速度从来不是这个方案的问题。
对，比如所有 linkedin.com/in/ 开头的链接前 8 个字符全一样，会全撞到同一个短码上，直接违反唯一性。
编码层能处理任意字符串，问题出在唯一性上，不在能不能编码。
浏览器只关心 URL 是否合法，不关心短码是怎么生成的，兼容性不是问题。
optionExplanations_en: Grabbing the first few characters is the simplest string op there is; speed was never the problem here.
Right — every link starting with linkedin.com/in/ shares the same first 8 characters, so they all collapse onto one code.
The encoding layer can handle any string; the failure is about uniqueness, not about whether it can be encoded.
Browsers only care whether the URL is well-formed, not how the code was generated, so compatibility was never at risk.
scenario: short.ly 的用户大量提交 www.linkedin.com/in/... 这种共享长前缀的 URL。
scenario_en: short.ly users submit huge numbers of URLs like www.linkedin.com/in/... that all share a long common prefix.

q: 为什么不直接用随机数生成器（如 Math.random()）生成短码？
q_en: Why not generate short codes directly with a random number generator such as Math.random()?
options: 生成一个随机数太耗费 CPU 资源
随机数结果没法用 base62 编码表示
随机数生成器只能产出偶数结果
熵不够，规模变大后短码碰撞概率会明显上升
why: 普通随机数生成器熵不够，存量 URL 增多后重复概率显著上升，每次都要查库验重。哈希函数的高熵输出是更好的「随机性来源」。
why_en: A plain random number generator lacks enough entropy to keep codes unique at scale, so collisions become likely as the URL count grows.
options_en: Generating a random number costs too much CPU.
A random number cannot be represented in Base62.
Random number generators only produce even numbers.
It lacks enough entropy, so collision probability rises noticeably as scale grows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量一个输出有多随机、多不可预测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Entropy measures how random and unpredictable an output is.

optionExplanations: 生成一个数字几乎不耗 CPU，性能从来不是普通随机数生成器的短板。
任何整数都能转成 Base62 字符串，编码本身没有限制。
标准随机数生成器输出的是均匀分布的整数，并不存在只出偶数这回事。
对，普通伪随机数生成器的熵不够高，短链存量变大后重复概率会明显上升，每次都要查库验重。
optionExplanations_en: Generating a single number costs almost no CPU; performance was never the weak spot of a plain RNG.
Any integer converts to a Base62 string just fine; encoding itself puts no limit on it.
A standard RNG outputs uniformly distributed integers — there is no such thing as it only producing even numbers.
Right — a plain PRNG lacks enough entropy, so as the URL count grows, repeat odds rise and every insert needs a uniqueness check.
scenario: short.ly 存量要从 100 万涨到 10 亿，写入路径不希望每次都靠查库重试保唯一。
scenario_en: short.ly grows from a million to a billion codes, and the write path should not depend on a lookup-and-retry loop for uniqueness.

q: 用 SHA-256 这类哈希函数生成短码，它提供的关键性质是？
q_en: What key properties does a hash function such as SHA-256 provide for short-code generation?
options: 确定性、固定长度输出、高熵（很少但不是零碰撞）
哈希输出保证绝对不会发生碰撞
哈希输出天然只有 6 个字符长
可以从哈希值直接反解出原始 URL
why: 哈希三性质：确定性、定长、高熵。注意它只是「很少」碰撞而非「不会」碰撞——这正是后面要处理的挑战。
why_en: A hash function gives determinism, a fixed-size output, and high entropy, though collisions are still possible rather than impossible.
options_en: Determinism, fixed-length output, and high entropy, though collisions are rare rather than impossible.
Hash output is guaranteed to never collide.
Hash output is naturally only six characters long.
You can reverse a hash value straight back to the original URL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把任意输入转换成固定长度、确定性输出的函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash function deterministically maps any input to a fixed-length output.

optionExplanations: 对，SHA-256 这类哈希给的是确定性、定长、高熵输出——碰撞很罕见，但从数学上永远不是零。
「绝对不会碰撞」是夸大的说法，鸽笼原理决定了任何定长哈希都存在理论碰撞。
SHA-256 原始输出是固定的 256 位，短码的 6 位是后续截断+编码的结果，不是哈希天生的长度。
哈希是单向函数，设计目的就是不可逆，反解不出原始输入是它的基本性质。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a hash like SHA-256 gives determinism, fixed-length output, and high entropy; collisions are rare but never mathematically zero.
'Never collides' overstates it — the pigeonhole principle guarantees any fixed-length hash has theoretical collisions.
SHA-256's raw output is a fixed 256 bits; a 6-character code comes from truncating and encoding it afterward, not its native length.
A hash is a one-way function by design — being unable to recover the input is its defining property, not a limitation.
scenario: short.ly 的多台 Write Service 不做全局协调，需要一个从长 URL 直接产出定长码的生成器。
scenario_en: short.ly's write services coordinate with nobody, so they need a generator that turns a long URL straight into a fixed-length code.

scenario: 你把哈希输出变成短码，但短码要能安全放在 URL path 里，并尽量紧凑。
scenario_en: You are turning hash output into a short code that must be compact and safe to place inside a URL path.
q: 应该使用哪种编码更合适？
q_en: Which encoding is the better fit?
options: Base64，直接保留 + 和 / 两个符号
十六进制，因为它的字符集最大
Base62：62 个字母数字字符，避开特殊符号
原始二进制字节，直接拼进 URL
why: Base62 比十六进制更紧凑，同时避开 Base64 里的 / 和 +；前者会和路径分隔冲突，后者在查询串里可能被解释为空格。
why_en: Base62 is compact and URL-safe because it avoids Base64 characters like slash and plus.
whenOtherWins: 如果短码不放在 URL path 中，而是内部二进制 token，原始 bytes 或 Base64URL 也可能更合适。
options_en: Base64, keeping the plus and slash characters as-is.
Hexadecimal, because it has the largest character set.
Base62: 62 letters and digits, avoiding special characters.
Raw binary bytes appended directly to the URL.
tradeoff: 更紧凑的编码 vs 更大字符集但更长的编码

termDefinitions.meaning: 只用 a-z、A-Z、0-9 共 62 个字符表示数字的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Base62 represents numbers using only the 62 letters and digits a-z, A-Z, and 0-9.

optionExplanations: Base64URL 变体（把 + / 换成 - _）才适合放进路径，原始 Base64 的 + 和 / 会和 URL 语法冲突。
十六进制只有 16 个字符，同样信息编出来的字符串明显更长，牺牲了紧凑性换可读性。
对，Base62 只用字母数字这 62 个字符，比十六进制紧凑，又天然避开 Base64 里会惹麻烦的 + 和 /。
原始字节里可能包含不可打印或需要转义的字符，直接塞进 URL 路径会被浏览器解析出错。
optionExplanations_en: The Base64URL variant (swapping + / for - _) belongs in a path; raw Base64’s plus and slash clash with URL syntax.
Hex only has 16 characters, so encoding the same information takes visibly more characters — compact traded for readable.
Right — Base62 uses just the 62 letters and digits, more compact than hex, and it skips the plus and slash that trip up Base64.
Raw bytes can contain unprintable or escape-needing characters, which would break URL parsing if dropped straight in.

q: 补全 Base62 的字符集选择：
q_en: Fill in the character set used by Base62.
why: 短链码通常出现在 URL path 里，字符越紧凑越好，但不能引入 path separator 或容易被转义的字符。
why_en: Base62 uses letters and digits while excluding URL-problematic slash and plus characters.

q: 这对短码位数和碰撞处理策略意味着什么？
q_en: What does this imply for short-code length and collision handling?
options: 必须每次生成都改用 16 位短码才安全
编码空间足够大，可以完全跳过数据库唯一约束检查
218 万亿远超存量，8 位短码够用很久，约束+重试兜底
存量增长后应立刻切换到 UUID 作为短码
why: 218 万亿远超十亿级存量，8 位 Base62 短码空间还够用很久；仍要靠 UNIQUE 约束兜底碰撞，但不必现在就加长短码。
why_en: 218 trillion possible codes dwarf a billion-URL scale, so 8-character Base62 codes have plenty of headroom and still need a UNIQUE constraint as the collision safety net.
scenario: 8 位 Base62 编码给出约 62^8 ≈ 218 万亿种组合，你的服务当前存量约几十亿条短链。
scenario_en: Eight Base62 characters give about 62^8, or roughly 218 trillion combinations, while your service stores only a few billion short links today.
options_en: We must switch to 16-character codes right away for safety.
The code space is big enough that we can skip the database uniqueness check.
218 trillion dwarfs the current scale, so 8 characters last a long time with a constraint plus retries as the backstop.
We should switch to UUID short codes as soon as the count grows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 62 个字母数字字符表示数字的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Base62 encodes numbers using 62 letters and digits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库约束，保证某列的值不会重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UNIQUE constraint stops a database column from holding duplicate values.

optionExplanations: 16 位短码更长，牺牲了短链的核心卖点，而 8 位空间目前完全够用，没必要现在就加长。
空间大只是降低碰撞概率，不是消灭碰撞可能，唯一约束这道保险丝不能省。
对，62 的 8 次方接近两百二十万亿种组合，十亿级数据量根本用不完这个空间，唯一约束配重试足够兜底。
UUID 通常 32+ 位，远比 Base62 短码长，为了防一个概率很低的碰撞牺牲「短」，不划算。
optionExplanations_en: A 16-character code is longer, sacrificing the whole point of being short, while 8 characters still have plenty of headroom.
A big code space lowers collision odds, it does not eliminate them — the uniqueness constraint is still the safety net.
Right — 62^8 is about 218 trillion, dwarfing the billion-URL scale, so 8 characters last long with a constraint plus retries as backstop.
UUIDs typically run 32+ characters, far longer than a Base62 code — giving up 'short' to guard a low-odds collision is not worth it.

q: 截取哈希前 N 位作为短码的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of truncating the first N characters of a hash as the short code?
options: 同一个 URL 每次哈希会得到不同结果
N 越短编码空间越小，存量变多后碰撞概率上升
哈希后的结果没法做 Base62 编码
生成的短码没办法存进数据库
why: 哈希输出高熵但不是无限空间；截断后只有固定大小的 code space，随着已有 code 数量增加，新 code 撞上的概率约为 n / |S|。
why_en: Truncating a hash limits the code space, so collision probability rises as more codes are stored.
options_en: Hashing the same URL twice gives a different result each time.
The shorter N is, the smaller the code space, so collision odds rise as more codes are stored.
A hash output cannot be Base62 encoded.
The generated short code cannot be saved to the database.
optionExplanations: 哈希函数是确定性的，同一个输入（不加盐的话）每次都得到相同输出，不存在这个问题。
对，截断后可用的 code space 是固定的 62^N 种，随着已存短码数量增加，新码撞上旧码的概率跟着上升。
哈希字节可以正常做 Base62 或任何编码，截断长度不影响编码能力。
生成出来的短码就是普通字符串，存进数据库列没有任何技术障碍。
optionExplanations_en: A hash function is deterministic — the same input (without a salt) always gives the same output, so this is not the risk.
Right — truncating fixes the usable code space at 62^N, and as more codes get stored, the odds a new one collides climb.
Hash bytes encode into Base62 or any other scheme just fine; truncation length does not limit what you can encode.
The generated code is just an ordinary string; there is no technical barrier to storing it in a database column.
scenario: short.ly 用 SHA-256 截前 8 位当短码，存量计划从 100 万涨到 10 亿。
scenario_en: short.ly takes the first 8 characters of a SHA-256 hash as the code, with volume planned to grow from a million to a billion.

scenario: 你采用哈希截断生成短码，数据库插入时发现 short_code 已存在。
scenario_en: You generate short codes by truncating a hash, and a database insert finds that the short_code already exists.
q: 最合理的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable way to handle this?
options: 直接覆盖掉已存在的旧映射
忽略这次冲突错误，照样返回该短码
先把旧的那条 URL 记录删掉
靠 UNIQUE 约束捕获冲突，加盐重试
why: 唯一约束是最终防线；冲突时用 salt/nonce 改变输入后重试，既保证唯一性，也避免把两个长 URL 指到同一个短码。
why_en: A unique constraint catches collisions, and bounded retries with a salt or nonce produce a different code safely.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务明确要求同一长 URL 永远复用同一短码，可以先做 canonical URL 查重并返回旧记录，而不是生成新码。
options_en: Overwrite the existing mapping directly.
Ignore the conflict error and return that code anyway.
Delete the old URL record first.
Let the UNIQUE constraint catch the conflict and retry with a salt.
tradeoff: 运行时唯一约束兜底 vs 提前隔离取值空间
codeSample:
INSERT INTO short_links (short_code, long_url, salt)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3)
ON CONFLICT (short_code) DO NOTHING
RETURNING short_code;
-- 返回 0 行 = 撞码；换 salt 后重新算 short_code 再插入。

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库列级约束，插入重复值时会报错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UNIQUE constraint makes the database reject an insert that would duplicate an existing value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加进哈希输入的额外随机值，让同一输入能产生不同哈希结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A salt or nonce is extra randomness mixed into a hash input so the same input can produce a different output.

optionExplanations: 覆盖会把别人已经发出去的短链指向别的地址，是破坏性操作，不能作为默认冲突处理。
忽略冲突会让一个短码同时对应两条长 URL，谁的重定向生效变成随机的，这是数据错误。
删掉一条无关用户的记录来给自己腾位置，是把冲突代价转嫁给了别人的数据。
对，让数据库的 UNIQUE 约束兜底捕获冲突，加个 salt 重新算一次短码再插入，既安全又不破坏已有数据。
optionExplanations_en: Overwriting redirects someone else’s already-shared link to a different address — destructive, not a default conflict handler.
Ignoring the conflict leaves one code pointing at two long URLs; whichever wins the redirect is random — that is data corruption.
Deleting an unrelated user's record to free the slot just shifts the cost of your conflict onto someone else's data.
Right — let the UNIQUE constraint catch the conflict, then salt the input and recompute the code before inserting again.

q: 哈希方案和递增计数器方案的关键取舍有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which tradeoffs matter between hash-based and incrementing-counter short-code generation?
options: 哈希方案可能碰撞，需要唯一约束和重试
计数器天然唯一，但需要全局协调计数值
计数器短码可能可预测，存在枚举风险
哈希方案不需要任何数据库写入
why: 哈希的难点是碰撞和查重；计数器的难点是协调和可预测性。两者都需要把 short_code 到 long_url 的映射写入持久存储。
why_en: Hashing trades collision handling for less coordination, while counters trade uniqueness for coordination and predictability concerns.

rows: 无需全局序列，输出高熵
可能碰撞，依赖 UNIQUE + 重试

tradeoff: 哈希省协调但可能碰撞 vs 计数器唯一但需全局协调
options_en: Hashing can collide, so it needs a uniqueness constraint and retries.
A counter is naturally unique, but requires global coordination of the counter value.
Counter-based codes can be predictable, creating an enumeration risk.
Hashing needs no database writes at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局递增的整数序列，每次取值都不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counter is a globally incrementing integer sequence that yields a new value each time.

optionExplanations: 哈希方案的代价：即使高熵，截断后仍有非零碰撞率，得靠 UNIQUE 约束和重试兜底。
计数器的代价：天然不撞码，但所有 Write Service 实例得从同一个源头取号，多了一层协调依赖。
计数器的另一个代价：相邻整数编码出的短码彼此可猜，攻击者能顺着遍历挖到未公开的链接。
两种方案都得把这份映射持久化到数据库里，哈希方案同样要写库，并不能省掉这一步。
optionExplanations_en: Hashing's cost: even at high entropy, truncation leaves a nonzero collision rate, so you still need a UNIQUE constraint and retries.
The counter's cost: it never collides, but every Write Service instance has to draw from one shared source, adding coordination.
The counter's other cost: codes from adjacent integers are guessable, letting an attacker enumerate and find unshared links.
Both approaches still have to persist the short_code-to-long_url mapping to the database; hashing does not skip that step.
scenario: short.ly 每天新建 10 万条、存量 10 亿，要在哈希截断和 Redis 全局 counter 之间定一个方案。
scenario_en: short.ly adds 100k links a day against a billion stored and must settle between truncated hashing and a global Redis counter.

scenario: 你想完全避免短码碰撞，并且写入量并不高，可以接受一个全局序列来源。
scenario_en: You want to avoid short-code collisions entirely, write volume is low, and a global sequence source is acceptable.
q: 哪种短码生成方式最直接？
q_en: Which short-code generation method is the most straightforward fit?
options: 直接截取原始 URL 的前 N 个字符
全局递增 counter，做 Base62 编码
让每台应用服务器各自从 0 开始独立计数
每次随机生成一个 2 位短码
why: 全局递增 counter 每次返回不同整数，再 Base62 后得到紧凑短码，天然避免碰撞。关键是 counter 必须全局唯一，而不能每台机器各算各的。
why_en: A global incrementing counter encoded with Base62 produces compact codes with no collisions.
whenOtherWins: 如果不能接受可预测短码，或希望同一 URL 的短码由内容确定，哈希加盐方案会更自然。
options_en: Take the first N characters of the original URL directly.
A global incrementing counter, Base62-encoded.
Let each application server count up from zero, independently.
Randomly generate a 2-character code each time.
tradeoff: 计数器零碰撞 vs 需要一个全局协调的序列来源

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局递增的整数序列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counter is a globally incrementing integer sequence.

optionExplanations: 输入天然离散、几乎不共享前缀时前缀法还能凑合，但短链场景做不到这个假设，前缀相同的 URL 会撞码。
对，全局唯一序列换 Base62 编码，每次拿到的整数都不同，天然零碰撞，还不用查重。
多实例各算各的意味着不同机器很快各自数到同一个数字，短码立刻重复，等于没有全局唯一性。
2 位 Base62 只有 62^2 约 3844 种组合，稍有几百个短链就撞得飞起，空间小到不现实。
optionExplanations_en: A prefix works only when inputs are naturally distinct with no shared prefixes — URLs rarely satisfy that, so it collides.
Right — a single global sequence, Base62-encoded, gives a different integer every time: zero collisions, no dedup check needed.
Independent per-instance counting means different machines soon reach the same number, so codes duplicate almost immediately.
A 2-character Base62 code only has 62^2, about 3,844 combinations — a few hundred links in and you are already colliding.

q: Redis 为什么适合做全局 counter？
q_en: Why is Redis a good fit for a global counter?
options: INCR 是原子操作，能为并发请求返回不同值
Redis 会自动把短码写入 Postgres
Redis 只能单用户单连接访问，所以没有并发
Redis 不需要持久化任何状态
why: Redis 单线程处理命令且 INCR 原子递增；两个并发请求不会拿到同一个 counter 值。这正好解决多个 Write Service 实例共享序列的问题。
why_en: Redis INCR is atomic, so concurrent writers receive distinct counter values from one shared sequence.
options_en: INCR is atomic, so concurrent requests always get distinct values.
Redis automatically writes short codes into Postgres.
Redis only allows single-user, single-connection access, so there is no concurrency.
Redis needs no persisted state at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子自增命令，并发调用也不会返回重复值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR is Redis's atomic increment command, so concurrent calls never return the same value.

codeSample:
INCR bitly:counter
-- atomic +1; two concurrent callers get e.g. 100234 and 100235, never the same value
-- persisted via AOF (appendonly yes) so a restart does not reset the count
optionExplanations: 对，INCR 在 Redis 单线程事件循环里一次执行到底，两个并发请求永远拿不到同一个值。
Redis 只是发号器，把映射写进主数据库仍是应用代码自己负责的事，不会自动发生。
Redis 单线程处理命令不等于只服务一个客户端，成千上万个连接可以同时排队等命令执行。
计数器的值必须落盘或走 AOF/RDB 持久化，否则 Redis 重启后号码归零，会重复发出已用过的短码。
optionExplanations_en: Right — INCR runs to completion inside Redis's single-threaded event loop, so two concurrent callers never get the same value.
Redis is just the number dispenser; writing the mapping into the primary database is still the application’s job.
Single-threaded command processing does not mean single-client — thousands of connections can queue commands concurrently.
The counter value needs AOF or RDB persistence; without it a restart resets the count and starts reissuing used codes.
scenario: short.ly 有多个 Write Service 实例并发建链，短码必须全局唯一且生成不能加锁排队。
scenario_en: short.ly runs several write service replicas creating links concurrently; codes must be globally unique without serializing on a lock.

q_en: Fill in the capacity intuition for counter plus Base62 short codes.
text: {{1B}} 个 URL 用 Base62 表示仍约为 {{6}} 个字符；到 {{62^6}}（约 560 亿）才需要进入 7 位。

q: 递增 counter 生成短码的安全/隐私风险是什么？
q_en: What security or privacy risk comes from using an incrementing counter for short codes?
options: 递增计数器一定会产生短码碰撞
攻击者能枚举相邻短码，挖到未公开分享的 URL
生成的短码没办法被浏览器打开
数据库没法按 counter 值做查询
why: 连续 ID 经过 Base62 后仍可能被猜到相邻值，攻击者可以遍历短码。可用 secret XOR/可逆混淆、随机化范围或接受公共分享语义来权衡。
why_en: Sequential counters can make codes enumerable, so an attacker may discover nearby URLs unless the sequence is obfuscated.
options_en: An incrementing counter is guaranteed to cause short-code collisions.
An attacker can enumerate nearby codes and discover URLs that were never shared publicly.
The generated short code cannot be opened in a browser.
The database cannot query by the counter value.
optionExplanations: 计数器天然递增不重复，碰撞恰恰是它不会有的问题，风险出在别的地方。
对，短码是连续整数编码出来的，攻击者顺着改一位数字遍历，就能挖到本该私密分享的链接。
Base62 输出的都是合法 URL 字符，浏览器打开没有任何障碍。
counter 值就是普通整数列，按它建索引查询和其他字段没有区别。
optionExplanations_en: An incrementing counter never repeats by design; collision is exactly the risk it does not have.
Right — since codes are consecutive integers, an attacker can tweak a digit and walk through them, finding links meant to stay private.
Base62 only emits valid URL characters, so nothing stops a browser from opening the resulting link.
The counter value is just a plain integer column; indexing and querying it works the same as any other field.
scenario: short.ly 上有大量「知道链接才能看」的私密分享链，短码来自递增 counter 的 Base62 编码。
scenario_en: short.ly hosts many unlisted share links protected only by obscurity, with codes coming from Base62 over an incrementing counter.

scenario: 重定向请求拿到 short_code 后，要在 10 亿行映射表里快速找到 long_url。
scenario_en: A redirect request receives a short_code and must quickly find its long_url in a billion-row mapping table.
q: 数据库表上最关键的设计是什么？
q_en: What is the most important database table design for this lookup?
options: 把 short_code 设为主键或至少建唯一索引
每次全表扫描查找 short_code
只按 long_url 建索引
把所有字段存成一个 JSON 字符串且不建索引
why: short_code 是读取路径的查找键，把它设为 primary key/unique index 既保证唯一，又把查询从全表扫描变成索引查找。
why_en: Indexing short_code, usually as the primary key, gives fast lookup and enforces uniqueness.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询模式主要是按 user_id 列出某用户创建的所有短链，还需要额外的 user_id 索引，但重定向路径仍看 short_code。
options_en: Make short_code the primary key or at least add a unique index on it.
Do a full table scan for short_code on every lookup.
Only index long_url.
Store every field as one JSON string with no index at all.
tradeoff: 索引查找的存储/写入代价 vs 全表扫描的读延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 表里能唯一标识一行、且自动带索引的列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A primary key is the column that uniquely identifies a row and is automatically indexed.

optionExplanations: 对，重定向按 short_code 查找，把它设成主键或唯一索引，查询直接从全表扫描变成 O(log n) 定位。
全表扫描只适合行数很少的表，十亿行规模下逐行比对，延迟会直接击穿 <100ms 目标。
long_url 索引服务的是去重或反查场景，重定向查的是 short_code，这个索引帮不上主路径。
JSON blob 适合少量灵活字段的场景，对高频 key lookup 来说既没法建索引也没法利用主键。
optionExplanations_en: Right — redirects look up by short_code, so making it the primary key or a unique index turns the query into an O(log n) lookup.
A full scan only works for small tables; checking rows one by one across a billion rows blows through the <100ms target.
An index on long_url serves dedup or reverse lookups; redirects query by short_code, so this index does not help the hot path.
A JSON blob suits a few flexible fields, but it cannot be indexed or use a primary key for a high-frequency key lookup.

q: 没有 short_code 索引时，重定向查找会退化成什么？
q_en: What does redirect lookup degrade into without an index on short_code?
options: 退化成接近 O(1) 的内存直接读取
退化成 full table scan，逐行检查
退化成自动命中附近的 CDN 边缘节点
退化成只读一行元数据就返回
why: 没有索引，数据库只能扫描映射表找匹配 short_code；数据到百万/十亿级后，这会直接破坏 <100ms 重定向目标。
why_en: Without an index, redirect lookup becomes a full table scan, which is too slow at large scale.
options_en: It degrades to a near-O(1) in-memory read.
It degrades to a full table scan, checking rows one by one.
It degrades to automatically hitting a nearby CDN edge node.
It degrades to reading just one metadata row and returning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐行检查整张表来找匹配数据，没有索引时的默认方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full table scan checks every row in a table to find matches, the default when there is no index.

optionExplanations: O(1) 内存直接读取说的是哈希表或缓存命中，没有索引的普通表查找达不到这个复杂度。
对，没有索引时数据库只能从第一行开始逐行比对 short_code，退化成 full table scan。
CDN 命中发生在请求到数据库之前的边缘层，跟数据库本身有没有索引是两件独立的事。
没有索引就定位不到具体是哪一行，只读一行元数据这个说法本身就不成立。
optionExplanations_en: O(1) in-memory reads describe a hash table or cache hit; an unindexed table lookup never reaches that complexity.
Right — without an index the database has no shortcut but to check short_code row by row from the start, a full table scan.
A CDN hit happens at the edge before the request even reaches the database; it is unrelated to whether the table has an index.
Without an index there is no way to pinpoint which single row it is; reading just one metadata row does not hold.
scenario: short.ly 的映射表有 10 亿行，重定向 P99 预算 100ms，每次跳转都要按 short_code 查一次。
scenario_en: short.ly's mapping table has a billion rows, every redirect looks up by short_code, and the P99 budget is 100ms.

q: 仅靠给 short_code 建索引，能撑住这个峰值吗？不能的话下一步是什么？
q_en: Can an index on short_code alone handle this peak, and if not, what comes next?
options: 能撑住，索引已经让查找变成 O(log n)，足够应对任何峰值
撑不住，应该放弃索引换成全表扫描
撑不住，应该把 short_code 改得更短来提速
撑不住，需要在数据库前加内存缓存，把大部分读挡在数据库外
why: 索引把查找降到 O(log n)，但单实例 IOPS 撑不住 60 万级峰值读；下一步是在数据库前加内存缓存。
why_en: Indexing brings lookups down to O(log n), but a single instance's IOPS cannot absorb a 600k-QPS peak, so the next step is an in-memory cache in front of the database.
scenario: 峰值场景下重定向读 QPS 能到 60 万级别，而单个数据库实例配合索引大约能扛约 10 万 IOPS。
scenario_en: At peak, redirect reads can reach about 600k QPS, while one indexed database instance handles roughly 100k IOPS.
options_en: Yes, the index already makes lookups O(log n), which is enough for any peak.
No, so we should drop the index and use a full table scan instead.
No, so we should shorten short_code further to speed things up.
No, we need an in-memory cache in front of the database to absorb most reads before they hit it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒输入输出操作数，衡量存储设备的读写吞吐能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IOPS is input/output operations per second, a measure of storage throughput.

optionExplanations: O(log n) 降低的是比较次数，不是单实例 IOPS 上限，60 万 QPS 峰值还是会打穿数据库。
放弃索引会让查找从 O(log n) 退化成全表扫描，延迟只会更差，方向反了。
短码长度影响的是存储和展示，不改变数据库能扛的 IOPS 上限，提速无从谈起。
对，内存缓存把绝大多数热点读挡在数据库前面，索引解决查找效率，缓存解决吞吐上限。
optionExplanations_en: O(log n) cuts comparisons, not a single instance's IOPS ceiling; a 600k-QPS peak would still blow through the database.
Dropping the index turns O(log n) lookups back into a full scan — latency only gets worse, the wrong direction entirely.
Code length affects storage and display, not the IOPS ceiling; shortening it buys no speed here.
Right — an in-memory cache absorbs most hot reads before the database; the index handles lookup, the cache handles throughput.

q: 补全读流量估算：
q_en: Fill in the read-traffic estimate.
text: {{100M}} DAU * 每人每天 {{5}} 次重定向 = {{500M}} 次/天，平均约 {{5.8k}} QPS；若按 100x 峰值，要设计到约 {{600k}} read/s。
why: 这个估算解释了为什么只靠数据库索引还不够：平均值可控，但峰值读流量非常高，需要缓存和边缘层分担。
why_en: The traffic estimate shows why indexed database reads still need caching for peak redirect load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，衡量系统需要承受的请求速率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS is queries per second, the rate of requests a system must handle.

scenario: 短链读写比约 1000:1，热门短码会被反复点击，数据库索引仍可能扛不住峰值读。
scenario_en: The URL shortener has about a 1000:1 read-write ratio, popular short codes are clicked repeatedly, and database indexes may still fail under peak reads.
q: 应在应用和数据库之间加入什么？
q_en: What should be added between the application and the database?
options: 加一层内存缓存，存短码到长链的映射
加一个只处理写入的 Kafka topic
上线一套更复杂的登录系统
每次请求都重新生成一遍短码
why: 读重系统的第一层优化是缓存映射：命中时直接从内存返回 long_url，miss 再查数据库并回填缓存。
why_en: An in-memory cache stores short-code mappings so popular redirects avoid database reads.
whenOtherWins: 如果读量很低、数据量很小，单库索引可能已经足够，先加缓存反而增加运维复杂度。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Client"] --> Read["Read Service"]
    Read --> Cache[("Redis / Memcached")]
    Cache -->|hit| Redirect["302 redirect"]
    Cache -->|miss| DB[("Mapping DB")]
    DB --> Fill["fill cache"]
    Fill --> Redirect
options_en: Add an in-memory cache layer that stores the short-code-to-long-URL mapping.
Add a Kafka topic that only handles writes.
Ship a more elaborate login system.
Regenerate the short code on every single request.
tradeoff: 缓存换读延迟 vs 引入失效和预热复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存里没有目标数据，必须回源查数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache miss means the data is absent from cache and must be fetched from the database.

optionExplanations: 对，热门短码被反复点击，内存缓存能直接命中返回，miss 才回源查库，把大部分读挡在数据库前。
队列适合削峰写入或异步任务，重定向是同步读请求，加个只处理写的队列帮不上这条读路径。
重定向不需要知道用户是谁，登录系统解决的是身份问题，跟查找延迟没关系。
短码到长链是固定映射，请求时重新生成会跟数据库里存的值对不上，直接破坏已发出去的链接。
optionExplanations_en: Right — popular codes get clicked repeatedly, so an in-memory cache answers hits directly and only falls back on a miss.
A queue is for smoothing write bursts or async work; a redirect is a synchronous read, so a write-only queue does not help.
A redirect doesn't need to know who the user is; login solves an identity problem, unrelated to lookup latency.
The code-to-URL mapping is fixed; regenerating it per request would no longer match the stored value, breaking every link out there.

q: 按正确顺序排列一次缓存 miss 的重定向流程：
q_en: Put the redirect flow for a cache miss in the correct order.
steps: 把查到的 short_code -> long_url 映射写回缓存
请求到达 Read Service，先查 Redis/Memcached
缓存未命中，Read Service 查询数据库索引
why: cache-aside 路径是先查缓存，miss 再查库，随后回填缓存并完成重定向。这样热门短码后续请求会直接命中缓存。
why_en: The cache-aside flow checks cache first, reads the database on a miss, fills the cache, and then redirects.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant R as Read Service
  participant Cache as Cache
  participant DB as DB
  C->>R: GET /{code}
  R->>Cache: get(code)
  Cache-->>R: miss
  R->>DB: lookup(code)
  DB-->>R: long_url
  R->>Cache: set(code, long_url)
  R-->>C: 302 Location
tradeoff: 先查缓存省数据库负载 vs 缓存未命中时多一跳查库延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存，未命中时再查数据库并回填缓存的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside means the app checks the cache first and, on a miss, reads the database and fills the cache.

q: 这个量级差距最支持哪条缓存设计判断？
q_en: Which cache design decision is best supported by this order-of-magnitude latency gap?
options: SSD 已经够快，不需要再引入内存缓存
HDD 和内存之间的访问延迟差距完全可以忽略不计
把热点映射放进内存缓存，能带来数量级的读延迟收益
只要把存储全部换成 SSD 就能达到内存缓存的效果
why: 内存比 SSD 快约 1000 倍、比 HDD 快约 10 万倍，这个量级差距正是给热点重定向加内存缓存的理由。
why_en: Memory is roughly 1,000 times faster than SSD and 100,000 times faster than HDD, and that gap is exactly why hot redirects deserve an in-memory cache.
scenario: 内存访问约 100 纳秒，SSD 约 0.1 毫秒，HDD 约 10 毫秒，量级依次拉开。
scenario_en: Memory access is about 100 nanoseconds, SSD is about 0.1 milliseconds, and HDD is about 10 milliseconds.
options_en: SSD is already fast enough, so there's no need to add an in-memory cache.
The latency gap between HDD and memory can be safely treated as negligible.
Putting hot mappings in an in-memory cache buys an order-of-magnitude latency win.
Switching all storage to SSD alone matches what an in-memory cache gives you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒输入输出操作数，衡量存储设备吞吐能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IOPS is input/output operations per second, a measure of storage throughput.

optionExplanations: SSD 比内存慢了大约 1000 倍，「已经够快」只是相对机械硬盘而言，热点读还是能感受到差距。
内存比 HDD 快了大约 10 万倍，这是数量级差距，说可以忽略不计是完全说反了。
对，内存读取比磁盘存储快了好几个数量级，把高频访问的短码放进内存缓存，延迟收益立竿见影。
SSD 依然比内存慢约 1000 倍，全换 SSD 只是缩小了差距，达不到内存缓存那个量级的收益。
optionExplanations_en: SSD is roughly 1,000 times slower than memory; 'fast enough' only holds relative to a spinning disk — hot reads still feel the gap.
Memory beats HDD by roughly five orders of magnitude; calling that gap negligible has it exactly backwards.
Right — memory is about 1,000x faster than SSD and 100,000x faster than HDD, so caching hot codes buys an order-of-magnitude win.
SSD is still roughly 1,000x slower than memory; switching everything to SSD narrows the gap but never reaches the cache’s order of magnitude.

q: 引入内存缓存后要主动处理哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: Which issues must you actively handle after adding an in-memory cache?
options: 缓存预热，冷启动时 miss 仍会打到数据库
缓存失效，尤其是 URL 过期或删除后不能返回旧 long_url
容量和淘汰策略，如 LRU
所有写入都必须停止
why: 缓存提升读性能，但带来预热、失效、容量和淘汰策略。短链较少更新，失效难度比通用可变数据低，但过期时间必须和 TTL 对齐。
why_en: Caching adds warmup, invalidation, capacity, and eviction concerns even in a mostly read-heavy URL shortener.
options_en: Cache warmup: on a cold start, misses still hit the database.
Invalidation: an expired or deleted URL must not keep returning the old long_url.
Capacity and eviction policy, such as LRU.
All writes must stop.
optionExplanations: 冷启动或节点重启时缓存是空的，这段时间的 miss 会集中打到数据库，得规划预热或容忍这段压力。
URL 一旦过期或被删除，缓存里的旧映射如果不失效，用户会被继续带到一个本该已经失效的地址。
内存有限装不下所有映射，得靠 LRU 这类策略决定谁被淘汰，不然热数据会被冷数据挤出去。
缓存只是加速读路径，写入依然正常落库，跟暂停写入完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Cache is empty on a cold start or restart, so misses pile onto the database during that window — plan warmup or absorb the load.
Once a URL lapses or gets deleted, a stale mapping left in cache keeps sending users to an address that should already be dead.
Memory cannot hold every mapping, so a policy like LRU decides who gets evicted, or cold data crowds out the data you need.
Caching only speeds up reads; writes still land in the database normally — nothing like pausing all writes.
scenario: short.ly 在数据库前加 Redis 缓存扛 10 万 QPS 读，而短链本身支持过期和删除。
scenario_en: short.ly puts Redis in front of the database to absorb 100k read QPS, while links themselves can expire or be deleted.
codeSample:
# 写入时缓存映射，TTL 必须 <= 短链自身过期时间
SET url:abc123 "https://www.linkedin.com/in/ashlyn" EX 2592000
# 读路径：命中直接跳，未命中回库并回填（冷启动仍会打 DB）
GET url:abc123
# 用户改目标或删链接时，必须主动失效，否则跳旧地址
DEL url:abc123
# 容量到顶时按 LRU 淘汰冷短码
CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru

scenario: 短链支持 expiration_date，某个 short_code 已经过期，但缓存里还有旧映射。
scenario_en: Short links support expiration_date, and one short_code has already expired while the cache still holds the old mapping.
q: 缓存 TTL 应该如何设置？
q_en: How should the cache TTL be set?
options: 永不过期，大幅减少数据库访问次数
TTL 应等于或短于剩余过期时间
统一设置成一个固定的 10 年
只依赖客户端浏览器本地缓存
why: 缓存项不能活得比 URL 本身更久，否则过期短链仍可能被重定向。TTL 对齐 expiration_date 是最直接的防 stale 策略。
why_en: Cache TTL must not outlive the URL expiration time or expired links can keep redirecting.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务不支持过期或删除，长 TTL 更可接受；如果要求立即撤销，还需要主动失效或版本化。
options_en: Never expire the entry, to drastically cut database access.
TTL should equal or be shorter than the URL's remaining validity window.
Set every TTL to a flat, fixed 10 years.
Only rely on the client's local browser cache.
tradeoff: TTL 越短越新鲜 vs TTL 越长数据库压力越小

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cache entry lives before it must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 缓存活得比 URL 本身还久，过期后仍会命中缓存返回旧映射，白白省了数据库访问却放出了错误结果。
对，TTL 卡在剩余有效期之内，缓存条目最晚跟 URL 同时到期，不会比 URL 本身活得更久。
10 年在实践中等同于永不过期，只是把「放出旧映射」的窗口拉得非常长，问题本质没变。
浏览器缓存只能减少这一个用户的重复请求，服务端缓存里的旧映射照样存在，问题根本没解决。
optionExplanations_en: A cache that outlives the URL keeps serving the stale mapping after it should be gone — saving hits at the cost of wrong answers.
Right — capping TTL at the remaining validity window means the cache entry lapses no later than the URL itself.
10 years is effectively never expiring in practice — it just stretches the 'stale mapping' window very long, same problem.
Browser caching only cuts repeat requests from that one user; the stale server-side cache entry is still there, untouched.

scenario: 用户分布全球，热门短码希望尽量靠近用户完成重定向，减少跨区域往返。
scenario_en: Users are global, and popular short codes should redirect as close to the user as possible to reduce cross-region round trips.
q: 可以引入哪一层优化？
q_en: Which optimization layer can be introduced?
options: CDN 边缘节点直接执行重定向逻辑
只是把数据库磁盘容量调大
让用户手动复制粘贴 long_url
把所有请求都固定发到单一区域主库
why: CDN PoP 可以缓存热门 short_code 映射，edge function 甚至能直接返回 redirect，避免请求回源到 Primary Server。
why_en: A CDN and edge function can serve popular redirects near users without reaching the origin service.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户集中在单区域、延迟目标宽松或成本敏感，应用层缓存可能已经足够，不必先上边缘计算。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    User["Global user"] --> Edge["CDN PoP / Edge function"]
    Edge -->|hit| Redirect["302 near user"]
    Edge -->|miss| Origin["Origin Read Service"]
    Origin --> Store[("origin cache / DB")]
    Origin --> Edge
options_en: A CDN with edge nodes running the redirect logic directly.
Just increase the database's disk capacity.
Have users manually copy and paste the long_url.
Route every request to a single-region primary database.
tradeoff: 边缘就近响应换低延迟 vs 边缘失效/运维复杂度和成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 运行在 CDN 边缘节点上的代码，能在离用户最近的地方处理请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge function is code that runs on CDN edge nodes, handling requests close to the user.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN 在某个地理位置部署的边缘接入点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PoP (point of presence) is a CDN's edge location in a given geographic area.

optionExplanations: 对，把热门映射放到离用户最近的边缘节点，跳转逻辑就地执行完，不用每次都跑一趟回源，省下跨洲往返。
磁盘容量解决的是存不存得下的问题，跟请求要跑多远、跨几个大洲完全是两个维度。
人工复制粘贴牺牲了产品最核心的一键跳转体验，只能算临时补救，不是常规方案。

optionExplanations_en: Right — a popular mapping can live at the CDN edge nearest the user, and the edge function redirects before reaching the origin.
Disk capacity is about whether the data fits, an entirely different axis from how far a request travels across continents.

q: CDN/edge redirect 的代价包括哪些？（多选）

options: 全局缓存失效和一致性更复杂
边缘函数有执行时间、内存和依赖限制
调试和监控比中心化服务更难
它会让所有短码立刻变长
why: 边缘层用成本和复杂度换延迟：失效、资源限制、观测性和费用都要讨论。它不会改变短码本身长度。
why_en: Edge redirects trade latency for more complex invalidation, runtime limits, monitoring, and cost.
options_en: Global cache invalidation and consistency become more complex.
Edge functions have execution time, memory, and dependency limits.
Debugging and monitoring are harder than with a centralized service.
It makes every short code instantly longer.
optionExplanations: 映射改了或失效了，得让分布在全球的每个边缘节点都同步更新，协调成本比单一数据库高得多。
边缘运行时通常有严格的执行时长、内存上限和可用依赖清单，复杂逻辑塞不进去。
请求分散到几十上百个边缘节点，出问题时定位是哪个节点、哪次部署出的错要费更多工夫。
边缘部署改变的是重定向发生的位置，短码本身的生成方式和长度完全不受影响。
optionExplanations_en: Once a mapping changes or lapses, every edge node scattered worldwide needs that update — far more coordination than one database.

With requests spread across dozens of edge nodes, pinpointing which node and deployment caused an issue takes more digging.
Edge deployment changes where the redirect happens, not how codes are generated or how long they are.

q: 这个存储量级对数据库架构选择意味着什么？
q_en: What does this storage size imply for the database architecture choice?
options: 500GB 已经远远超过单机容量，必须从第一天就做分片
500GB 单实例数据库能轻松容纳，不必一开始就分片
这个量级下必须放弃关系型数据库，全面改用列式存储
存储量级这么大，建索引已经没有意义
why: 500GB 对现代 SSD 和单个数据库实例都不是问题；除非真的碰到硬件瓶颈，否则不必一开始就分片。
why_en: 500 GB is not a problem for a modern SSD or a single database instance, so sharding isn't necessary until a real hardware limit shows up.
scenario: 按每行约 500 bytes 估算，10 亿条短链映射总共约需 500GB 主数据存储。
scenario_en: At about 500 bytes per row, one billion short-link mappings require roughly 500 GB of primary data storage.
options_en: At 500 GB we already exceed single-machine capacity, so sharding is required from day one.
500 GB fits comfortably on a single database instance, so sharding is not needed on day one.
At this scale we must abandon relational databases entirely for columnar storage.
At this scale, indexing no longer makes sense.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据切分到多台机器存储，用来突破单机容量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across multiple machines to get past a single machine's capacity limit.

optionExplanations: 500GB 对现代硬盘来说只是零头，远远够不上「超过单机容量」，分片在这个阶段是过度设计。
对，500GB 一个数据库实例就能轻松扛住，除非真的碰到实测的硬件瓶颈，不必现在就分片。
500GB 加上事务和索引需求，关系型数据库处理得游刃有余，换列式存储解决的是分析型大宽表场景。
存储量级大反而更需要索引——没有它，十亿行规模下的每次查找都要付出线性扫描的代价。
optionExplanations_en: A 500 GB is a rounding error for a modern disk, nowhere near exceeding single-machine capacity — sharding here is over-engineering.
Right — 500 GB fits comfortably on one database instance; sharding is not needed until you hit an actual hardware limit.
At 500 GB with transactional and indexing needs, a relational database handles this easily; columnar stores solve a different problem.
A larger dataset makes indexing more necessary, not less — without it every lookup across a billion rows pays for a linear scan.

scenario: 短链系统读流量已由缓存承担，创建新短链每天约 100k，写入吞吐很低。
scenario_en: Reads are handled by cache, and the system creates about 100k new short links per day, so write throughput is low.
q: 数据库选择上最务实的答案是什么？
q_en: What is the most pragmatic database choice here?
options: 只能选 Cassandra，别的数据库都写不了
只能选图数据库来存这份映射
大多数成熟数据库都可以，Postgres 是合理默认
这个场景根本不需要持久化数据库
why: 写入量约 1 row/s，读峰值被缓存分担，Postgres/MySQL/DynamoDB 等都能做。面试里选自己熟悉且能解释 HA/索引/备份的数据库更重要。
why_en: Once reads are cached and writes are low, many databases work, with Postgres being a reasonable default.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求变成极高写入、多区域本地写或弱一致可接受，DynamoDB/Cassandra 这类方案可能更有优势。
options_en: Only Cassandra can handle the writes here.
Only a graph database can store this mapping.
Most mature databases can do this; Postgres is a reasonable default.
This scenario doesn't need a persistent database at all.
tradeoff: 选熟悉的数据库换开发效率 vs 为未来极端写入预留专用数据库

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的开源关系型数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向海量写入和多区域场景的宽列存储数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column database built for very high write throughput and multi-region deployments.

optionExplanations: 写入量约 1 row/s 这种低负载下，Cassandra 的高写吞吐能力根本用不上，选它是资源浪费。
图数据库擅长的是多跳关系遍历，这里只是 code 到 URL 的一次性直接查找，用不上图结构。
对，这个负载水平下，几款主流数据库都能扛住，挑一个自己吃得透、能讲清高可用和索引设计的更实际。
映射必须能在重启和故障后还在，缓存只是加速层，不能替代持久化存储。
optionExplanations_en: At roughly 1 row/s of write load, Cassandra's high-write-throughput strength never gets exercised — picking it is overkill.
Graph databases shine at multi-hop relationship traversal; this is a single direct code-to-URL lookup, no graph needed.
Right — with low writes and cached reads, Postgres, MySQL, or DynamoDB all work; pick whichever you can defend HA and backups on.
The mapping has to survive restarts and failures; a cache only speeds things up, it cannot replace durable storage.

scenario: 读请求远多于写请求，读路径是 GET /{short_code}，写路径是 POST /urls。
scenario_en: Read requests far outnumber writes: the read path is GET /{short_code}, and the write path is POST /urls.
q: 服务层如何拆分更利于独立扩展？
q_en: How should the service layer be split to scale independently?
options: 把 Read/Write Service 拆开，各自独立扩容
所有请求固定打到同一个实例
只留 Write Service，重定向交给客户端处理
把数据库拆成多张没有索引的表
why: 读写负载差异巨大时，拆分服务可让 redirect path 大规模横向扩展，而写路径保持较小规模并专注短码生成。
why_en: Separating read and write services lets the high-volume redirect path scale independently from the low-volume creation path.
whenOtherWins: 在早期低流量系统里，一个服务更简单；等读写负载和团队运维能力需要时再拆。
options_en: Split Read Service and Write Service apart so each scales independently.
Pin every request to the same single instance.
Keep only the Write Service and let the client handle redirects.
Split the database into multiple tables with no indexes.
tradeoff: 读写分离换独立扩容能力 vs 多一层服务拆分和路由复杂度
optionExplanations: 对，读写负载差几个数量级时，拆开服务能让重定向那条高流量路径单独横向扩容，不必带着写路径一起扩。
单实例扛不住重定向那种高并发读流量，早晚会在某个 QPS 阈值上被打垮。
重定向要查数据库才知道目标地址，客户端手里没有这份映射，做不了这件事。
拆表不解决查找效率问题，没有索引的表无论拆成几张，逐行扫描的代价还在。
optionExplanations_en: Right — with read and write load orders of magnitude apart, splitting the services lets redirects scale on their own.
A single instance cannot absorb redirect-level concurrent reads; it will get overwhelmed past some QPS threshold.
A redirect needs the database to know the target address; the client never holds that mapping, so it cannot do this.
Splitting tables does not fix lookup efficiency — however many pieces, an unindexed table still pays for a row scan.

q: 按正确顺序排列 counter 方案下创建短链的写入流程：
q_en: Put the write flow for creating a short link with the counter approach in the correct order.
steps: Write Service 把 counter 值编码成 Base62 短码
用户提交 long_url 到 POST /urls
Write Service 向 Redis INCR 获取全局唯一 counter
把 short_code、long_url、expiration_date 写入数据库并返回 short_url
why: 写路径先接收请求，再拿全局唯一 ID，编码为短码，最后持久化映射并返回给用户。
why_en: The write path receives the URL, gets a unique counter, encodes it, stores the mapping, and returns the short URL.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant W as Write Service
  participant R as Redis
  participant DB as DB
  C->>W: POST /urls
  W->>R: INCR counter
  R-->>W: next id
  W->>W: base62(id)
  W->>DB: insert mapping
  W-->>C: short_url
tradeoff: 预先批量取号段省网络调用 vs 单次 INCR 实现简单

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子自增命令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR is Redis's atomic increment command.

q: 更高级别答案里，counter 方案还应补充哪些生产化细节？（多选）
q_en: Which production-readiness details should a stronger counter-based design include?
options: counter batching：每个 Write Service 申请一批号段，减少 Redis 网络调用
Redis Sentinel/Cluster：避免 counter 服务成为无保护单点
多区域 disjoint counter ranges：各区域本地写，避免跨区域协调
要求所有区域都从 counter=0 开始，方便调试
why: 号段批量、Redis 故障转移、多区域互斥范围是 counter 方案走向生产时的关键补强。所有区域从 0 开始会直接制造重复短码。
why_en: Production counter designs add batching, Redis failover, and disjoint regional ranges to reduce calls and preserve uniqueness.
options_en: Counter batching: each Write Service instance requests a batch of values, cutting Redis network calls.
Redis Sentinel/Cluster: avoids the counter service becoming an unprotected single point of failure.
Disjoint counter ranges per region: each region writes locally, avoiding cross-region coordination.
Require every region to start its counter at 0, for easier debugging.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的高可用方案，主节点故障时自动切换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Sentinel and Cluster provide automatic failover when the primary Redis node fails.

optionExplanations: 每次创建都单独找 Redis 要一个号，网络往返成本会随写入量线性增加，批量取一段号省下大部分调用。
counter 全靠单个 Redis 实例发号，它一挂全局创建流程就跟着停摆，加故障转移能补上这个单点。
跨区域每次都回中心节点抢号会拖慢延迟，给各区域分配互不重叠的号段就能各自本地写不用协调。
所有区域从 0 开始等于让不同区域各自独立生成一样的号码，最先落库的映射会互相覆盖或冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Asking Redis for one number per creation makes round trips scale linearly with writes; a batch of values cuts most of that.
If a single Redis instance is the only number source, it going down halts creation entirely; failover closes that single point.
Racing back to one central node for every number adds latency; a non-overlapping range per region lets it write locally.
Starting every region at zero means they would independently generate the same numbers, so mappings collide or overwrite.
scenario: short.ly 的 Redis counter 方案要上生产：三个区域部署，每次 INCR 都是一次跨机网络往返。
scenario_en: short.ly's Redis counter design is going to production across three regions, where every INCR costs a network round trip.
codeSample:
# 号段批量：一次拿 1000 个，Redis 网络往返减少到 1/1000
INCRBY counter:us-east 1000   -> 1234000
# 本实例在内存里发放 1233001..1234000，用完再申请
# 多区域各持一段互斥范围，本地写不跨区协调
INCRBY counter:eu-west 1000   -> 5001000
# counter 服务本身不能是裸单点
SENTINEL monitor counter-master 10.0.0.5 6379 2
